title: We found a hornbill nest
storyboard: Film: naturalist whispering at a safe distance from a hornbill nest tree; long-lens shot of the sealed slit

scenes.headline: We found a hornbill nest. We're staying back.
The nest hole is sealed with mud
scenes.body: Only a narrow slit stays open. The male passes food through it to the female inside.

scenes.headline: See the ridge on the bill?
scenes.body: That helmet-like ridge on some hornbills is called a casque.

scenes.headline: Our nest rule
scenes.body: Watch from far away, keep it short, never point people to the tree.

caption:
This tree has a family sealed inside it.

In almost every hornbill species (ground hornbills are the exception), the nest is walled in with mud; after the eggs hatch the female breaks out, and the chicks may be sealed in again.

Source: Britannica, Hornbill. Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Storyboard: naturalist PIP and nest-tree shots to be filmed by us; CC photo/video stand in. Shows ethical fieldcraft (distance, no location) as part of the content.
